title: Ethnic Bias Data Explorer
subtitle: Calling for transparency in ethnic data and reporting

about.heading: About
about.ee_heading: What do we mean by ‘ethnic European’?
about.europhobia: Ethnic Europhobia is the precise term for antiwhite bias against people of ethnic European heritage. Official statistics and news coverage often use the broader label ‘White’, which can mix different groups together. Using this term keeps the claim specific and testable against the heritage data this project assembles.

term.ee_tip: Ethnic Europeans are people whose ancestry traces to the native peoples of Europe, often called ‘White’.

method.scale_intro: Each harm is scored out of 100. Heritage counts for most of the score. Full marks require separately identifying ethnic Europeans, not only a broader category such as White, or a proxy such as nationality.
method.cap_applied_body: The uncapped total is {uncapped}%. A country with no real ethnicity data is capped at 25%.
method.previous: On the previous rubric this country scored {score}%.
method.previous_with_band: On the previous rubric this country scored {score}% ({band}).
method.previous_weights: Harm weights changed on {date}. With the earlier weights (sexual abuse 25%, the other five harms 15% each) this country scored {score}%.
method.colours: Map colours: {bands}. Scores are reviewed as new data is found (last review {date}).
method.gold: 100% means a country publishes data that separately identifies ethnic Europeans, both as perpetrators (so one can tell when they disproportionately harm a group) and as child victims (so one can tell when ethnic European children are disproportionately harmed), alongside every other group, linked victim to perpetrator, for every harm.
method.cap: Proxies such as nationality or migration background earn at most one quarter of the heritage points. A published “White” category that merges Hispanic people or another group, so ethnic Europeans cannot be isolated, is also scored as a proxy under the same cap. A country with no real ethnicity data is capped at 25%, however complete its other counting is.
method.weights: The country score is a weighted average of the six harms: homicide 25%, sexual abuse 20%, sex trafficking 20%, physical abuse 15%, online exploitation 10% and neglect 10% (weights in use since 19 November 2026).
method.comp_victim_full: Published by harm, with ethnic Europeans identified separately — not only a broader category such as White, or a proxy such as nationality.
method.comp_other_full: Broad coverage, a low share of unknowns, rates per 100,000, victim–perpetrator linkage, and public, timely release.

media.title: Media coverage
media.lede: How news coverage of interracial violence between ethnic Europeans (White) and Black people compares with official offending-rate baselines. The map shows the Antiwhite media bias index. Countries not yet measured are marked pending.
media.load_error: The media data could not be loaded.
media.toggle_to_antiblack: Show as Antiblack media bias index
media.toggle_to_antiwhite: Show as Antiwhite media bias index
media.signed_plus_hint: Plus means White-on-Black coverage is over-represented relative to the baseline.
media.signed_minus_hint: Minus means Black-on-White coverage is over-represented relative to the baseline.
media.insufficient_hint: The index is undefined when there are no covered White–Black pair incidents.
media.completeness_desc: How completely official statistics record the ethnicity of child victims and offenders (0–100). This is the same score as on the Crime tab. It does not score how well children are protected.
media.legend_hatch_note: Hatching marks a lower bound, not a point estimate; the colour shows the country’s minimum bound.
media.map_note_one: Only {country} has been measured so far.
media.map_note_other: Only {n} countries have been measured so far: {list}.
media.table_h: Antiwhite media bias index by country, 2023 keyword sample
media.table_desc: One row per country. A point-estimate index is published when both directions are observed. A zero cell is shown as 0 of N plus the exact one-sided 95% lower bound, with the exact test p. The index is undefined only when there are no covered White–Black pair incidents. Pending means not yet measured.
media.ee_index_pending: Pending. This index has not been published yet.
media.sig_not_a_finding: Exact test p = {p}; not published as a finding, because the 2023 keyword sample is not a valid test of coverage.
media.rule_strict_hint: Race must be stated as White or Black in the article. A “white supremacist” or “white nationalist” label is not enough.
media.rule_broad_hint: A “white supremacist” or “white nationalist” label, or “espoused White supremacist beliefs”, counts as White. Liking or sharing such content does not.
media.method_note_h: Homicide and non-fatal violence, United States, 2023 keyword sample
media.method_note_desc: Homicide stories are compared with FBI Supplementary Homicide Reports (SHR) Expanded Homicide Data Table 6 (single victim/single offender, 2023). Non-fatal violence is compared with the National Crime Victimization Survey (NCVS). The two are not pooled into one index. This is a keyword-matched story sample, not a random sample of incidents.
media.sample_h: Sample size and date range, 2023 coded keyword sample
media.sample_desc: Stories and distinct incidents included after coding, with both races stated in the article. Incidents are counted once after merging duplicate IDs.
media.date_range: Dates of stories in the sample: {start} – {end}
media.frame_caveat: The keyword frame is a likely cause of the zero Black-on-White cell. Stories of interracial violence that never use the search phrases are outside the frame.
media.outlets_h: Coverage by outlet, included stories and incidents, 2023
media.outlets_desc: Point-estimate index cells are pending until an incident-based sample is complete. A zero cell is shown as 0 of N plus the exact one-sided 95% lower bound, not as a +0.5 multiplier.
media.col_total_hint: Media Cloud hits for the search phrases (volume only, not yet checked for relevance)
media.col_coded_hint: Hand-coded stories of those randomly sampled
media.baseline_shr_h: Homicide baseline: FBI SHR Table 6, 2023, single victim/single offender
media.baseline_shr_desc: Official counts of murder with known offender race, single victim and single offender. White-on-Black 324; Black-on-White 726. Table 6 has no victim-age breakdown, so child-specific claims cannot be made from this table. A per-capita rate view will sit next to these raw counts once a cited population denominator is joined; it is not yet available.
media.baseline_ncvs_h: Non-fatal violence baseline: NCVS violent incidents by offender and victim race
media.baseline_ncvs_desc: Bureau of Justice Statistics, National Crime Victimization Survey. Nonfatal violent incidents (rape or sexual assault, robbery, aggravated and simple assault); homicide is not covered. White and Black are non-Hispanic. Offender race is the victim's perception. These figures say nothing about motive and are not hate-crime counts.
media.baseline_comp: Not a strict time series: BJS changed how mixed Hispanic offender groups are classified in 2022, 2018 was published as percentages only, and BJS published no such table for 2020.
media.pct_only: {p}% of incidents against {v} victims (count not published)
media.disclosure_h: Disclosure track (not part of the index)
media.disclosure_desc: Whether each outlet named the group when it was knowable, measured separately from the index.
media.disclosure_pending: Not yet coded for the United States. The 2023 keyword sample cannot support this track: inclusion required race to be stated, so disclosure is 100% by construction.
media.stories_h: Sample stories, included in the 2023 coded set
media.stories_desc: Headline, outlet, date, direction, and how race was stated. Names of minors are not recorded.
media.methods_cdi: The CDI is the calculation behind the Antiwhite media bias index. It is used in methods only, not as a second public name. CDI = (White-on-Black media count ÷ Black-on-White media count) ÷ (White-on-Black baseline count ÷ Black-on-White baseline count). 1 means coverage is proportional to the baseline; above 1 means White-on-Black stories are over-represented; below 1 means Black-on-White stories are over-represented. When a cell is 0, a point estimate is not published.
media.src_stories: Coded stories, strict rule set ({year}, CSV)
media.src_stories_broad: Coded stories, broad rule set ({year}, CSV)
media.pairing: White / Black (race as stated in the article). ethnic Jewish, Palestinian, and similar labels are coded as other and are not in the index ratio.
media.tt_completeness: Ethnic data completeness: {score} — how completely official statistics record the ethnicity of child victims and offenders (0–100).
media.tt_insufficient: The index is undefined: no covered White–Black pair incidents.
